poems: The dishwasher starts its long argument with itself.

The worksheet has eleven problems.
We are on four.
Nobody is going to win this.
Bath water going gray around a plastic shark.

Rinse the sink.
Put the trash out.
Leave the porch light on for whoever is still driving.
At 8:04 the toddler requests water, a different blanket, and one more explanation of death.
A man on a treadmill in a garage, watching a game whose score he already knows.
Somewhere it is noon and a woman is deciding between soup and soup.

8:07. The afternoon coffee,
heard from at last.
The remote is under the middle cushion. It is always under the middle cushion.

A boy practices trumpet with a mute in,
which helps his family more than it helps him.
A blue recycling bin at the curb, lid propped open by a cereal box.
If it's a school night, the bargaining opens at 8:11 and closes badly.

Left on the stairs:
one sock
a library book
a charger
a plan
The dog goes and stands at the door and says nothing, and it is the loudest thing in the house.

8:14. Laundry warm out of the dryer,
briefly worth burying your face in.
A nurse coming on shift eats a sandwich standing up at 8:15, and that counts as dinner.
Somewhere two people sit on a porch not talking, both of them content, one of them pretending.
The pizza box will not fit in the trash and will not be broken down tonight.
“Teeth. Then a story. Then teeth again if you argue.”
A minivan idling outside a middle school gym, hatch open.
Nobody has drowned. The bath was a success.
At 8:21 a service asks whether we are still watching. We are, and we resent the question.

The project is due at some point.
Nobody has said the word diorama yet.
Bedtime. Approximately.

LOST DOG, the pole says, REWARD,
and a number worn soft by weather.
A kid gone limp on the couch, the negotiation over, and neither parent willing to move first.
A forklift beeping at an empty aisle.

8:27. Next door, the floodlight snaps on
for a possum with no agenda.
Just one more is a unit of time equal to eleven minutes.
A retired man carries the trash to the curb at 8:29, a full night early, on principle.
The kitchen has stopped producing food and started producing dishes.

Set out the cereal bowls.
It changes nothing.
Do it anyway.
Bath toys drained and lined along the tub edge like a small tired jury.
The first person to order a second drink at 8:33 sets the pace for the whole table.

8:34. Pajamas laid out in the shape
of a very flat child.
Somebody in this house has to make the lunches and it is going to be me.
A teenager laughing at a screen in a dark room, at nothing you will ever be told.
At 8:37 someone decides that tomorrow is the day they start.
The last practice of the night lets out and forty parents pull forward at once.

KEEP OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN,
printed on the one thing that would help.
Steam on the mirror, a handprint in it.
In another time zone a man is buttering toast and believes it is morning, because it is.

8:42. The garage could be reorganized tonight.
Could is carrying all of it.
A pot left soaking in the sink, a promise made to whoever gets up first.

Still to do:
lunches
one email
the thing you have been not doing
Wet hair on a pillowcase.
The homework is done in the sense that it is no longer being discussed.

8:47. The grill clicks as it cools,
retelling dinner.
At 8:48 the story ends and is immediately requested again.
Somebody's grandmother has been on the phone eleven minutes and has not gotten to the reason yet.
A clerk facing the soup aisle.
“I am not asleep, I am resting my eyes,” says a man who is asleep.
The trash goes out at 8:52 for a truck that comes at six. Call that faith.
A bike on its side in a yard.
The bar door opens and closes and the street gets one second of a song.

Bedtime, noun:
a time observed by no two people in the house equally.
You will not read the book. Put it on the nightstand anyway.
At 8:57 a woman at a bedside says goodnight to someone who cannot answer.

8:58. Three remotes, one working,
the working one missing.
Whatever was going to get done tonight has now been decided, quietly, by no one.
